themes.theme: The warrant is a constant, not a record. Every intent the POC names is a compile-time literal; the persisted record names none, and the observation never reads one.
Built vocabulary, no producer. The verdict types, chain states and 'reconciliation evidence absent' exist and are tested; nothing ever feeds them a computed or captured input.
The contract has one hole, and 10,971 items sit in it: orphaned-work Contradiction vs Unknown-provenance has no stated predicate.
The tracker links work to work, never work to intent. Item↔PR↔merge is recoverable at scale on Syzygy; requirement↔anything is ~0, and the contract forbids reading it from execution-side text anyway.

Independence is the scarce resource. Since D10 an agent row can warrant, adjudicate and declare; the gate lives in the worker's write set. The fifth answer is only worth having if who warrants, who verifies and what checks are kept apart mechanically.
Durability before coverage. Records the chain depends on live in a 0600 state-dir file; RFC4-16 and RFC8-26 require them Syzygy-owned and preserved from day one.

objections: U7 is V1 while V0 Trajectory is weak: true; it is ranked after the truth fixes and the join, and it is the only move that makes the fifth answer non-empty for anything.
An RFC amendment (U2) for a POC: without it the first real record (T7) puts one item in a recorded state and, read literally, 10,970 into an unfilterable Contradiction state.
U8 adds friction to every intent-bearing `bd create`: yes; it is the price of the owner's P-100 Q1 choice, and bugs warranted by an existing spec need only the requirement id.
Syzygy-on-Syzygy is self-grading: the gate is hosting-confirmed, the checker is pinned, verdicts carry mutants; the remaining risk is the separation question above.
U9 and U10 widen what P-100 Q1 chose: U10's rows are Syzygy records, arguably within it; U9 reads external_ref, which was Q1's option 2. Both are adoptions open to veto, and say so.

The V1 readiness drive's plans (syzygy-rrrd/qd2t/oq3x); its files are not in the repo — U7 may overlap it.
That GitHub merge_group SHAs equal main's commits in general; observed on one commit (c813f041c).
RFC4-13(a)/(b) and RFC3-16(a) were read in part (named-adapters.md:157-215 and the clause heads), not in full.
The P-100 packet itself (read only its DECISION-HISTORY rows); what the unread external_ref values hold on Butlers.
Whether syzygy-a4ry / syzygy-nosn already settle which merge-fact reading U9 should bind to.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: Ranking by fidelity under the accepted contracts (B2-F1, B2-F4, B2-F5, B2-F6): (1) a Syzygy materialization record naming proposal, item set and pinned revision — `recorded-identity`, the only form RFC2-18 binds a verdict to; (2) a declared `motivates` edge in a governance mapping artifact, adopted by a recorded act (RFC1-25 allows Requirement ref · Decision → Work item; SDR-4 makes governance mapping artifacts the primary declaration site) — honest, declared, but not a materialization, so RFC2-18's chain needs it treated as the pinned revision explicitly; (3) a tracker pointer Syzygy itself wrote (RFC4-17 `spec_id`) — re-derivable copy of (1), never authoritative; (4) a tracker field a worker wrote (spec_id 26/1370, metadata 37/1370 on Syzygy) — substrate annotation, asserted-by-worker, never a warrant (RFC8-23, RFC8-25); (5) requirement ids in commit subjects / PR bodies (1 of 500 subjects, 7 of 200 PR bodies on Syzygy) — execution-side prose, forbidden as a warrant source (RFC8-25), usable only as a hint for proposing a (2) row; (6) openspec tasks.md ↔ bead links (5 of 13 tasks.md name any bead, 7 mentions) — declared intent-side text, too sparse to matter; (7) similarity/title matching — forbidden (RFC8-22, RFC4-22 'never fuzzy-matched').

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: Coverage at scale vs honesty: only (1) and (2) are both honest and scalable. (1) scales forward only — it covers work created through Syzygy from now on, which is exactly P-100 Q1's chosen direction ('Syzygy's own creation records only'), provided the fleet creates work through a Syzygy path rather than raw `bd create`. (2) is the only honest backfill: batches of proposed rows, each adopted by a recorded act. (3)–(6) give coverage cheaply but cannot be warrants; their honest use is as candidate-generators for (2), with the candidate's evidence cited and nothing rendered as a warrant until adopted. The proving project's figures for (4)–(6) are [Unknown].

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: A declared warrant made after the work exists is a different fact from one recorded before it. Render the basis with its order: `recorded-at-materialization` (1), `declared-before-work` and `declared-after-work` (2, by comparing the adoption commit instant with the item's first commit or claim instant). A post-hoc warrant is honest only if labelled so; otherwise a backfill silently converts history into apparent plan. This is a rendering qualifier on the edge, not a new RFC1-25 relation (RFC1-26 needs an owner-decided amendment for a new relation).

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: Syzygy-on-Syzygy CAP1 is the natural first proving case, and Butlers is not. Syzygy has: 42 CAP1 requirement ids with exactly one conformance file each, each stating Case/Oracle/Falsifier (B3-F13); merge commits that carry hosting-confirmed check runs on the exact SHA (B3-F12, RFC4-13 route 2); recorded-identity item→PR links on 192 items (B3-F3); an owned repository (OWNED-REPOSITORIES.md row 1), so ledger writes are agent-decided; and cap1-core already ships the verdict vocabulary — ReconciliationFacts, computeReconciled, ChainState with `reconciled@${string}` (B1-F8). Butlers lacks a declared requirement→test mapping, its CI is [Unknown], and the POC's only test route is operator-reported (report-fact cap).
findings.where: u3 B3-F3, F12, F13; u1 B1-F8; .syzygy/governance/decisions/OWNED-REPOSITORIES.md:18-21

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: The gate is inside the worker's write set. A conformance file lives in the same repository the worker edits, so a merge whose CI is green can have weakened the check that 'verifies' it. Route 2 confirms the run happened on SHA M; it does not confirm the check is the one adopted for the requirement. A lawful verdict therefore needs the requirement → check mapping to pin the checker's blob digest (or a check version adopted by its own row before the merge), and must render Unknown(contradicted-pending-adjudication or missing-declaration) when the checker at M differs from the pinned one without an adoption. This is the same shape as RFC4-13(b)'s 'checker's definition is lawfully governed for that clause'.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: Job-level green is not per-requirement evidence. node-ci.yml produces job conclusions and uploads no per-test report (B3-F12). The minimum addition is a machine-readable per-test report (vitest JSON or JUnit) uploaded as a workflow artifact on merge_group, whose artifact id, digest and run id the observation captures (RFC4-13(a): the confirmation 'is a captured artifact inside snapshot identity … never a query re-run against the provider at some later read'). Captured into the repo or a Syzygy-owned store, it survives GitHub's artifact expiry (RFC8-27).

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: This is V1 work by the contract's own staging: RFC8-29 'V1 computes the reconciliation evaluation'; RFC2-19 'V1 computes'; v1.md V1 'Gap computation … Provenance surfaces — structured summaries linking each unit of work to the spec and vision that motivated it'. Starting it is 'when implementation starts', an agent decision under VIS-4; the V1 readiness drive (syzygy-rrrd/qd2t/oq3x) is the in-flight owner of V1 sequencing and its files are not in the repo [Unknown whether it already plans this].

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: None of RFC8-8's three planes is rendered. Plane (a) needs the set of approved normative claims; the POC follows one seeded OpenSpec change (B1-F9). Plane (b) needs `.syzygy/work/**`, which exists in neither Syzygy's tree (B2-F11) nor, as far as the POC reads, Butlers'. Plane (c) is the board, without the record check (run-1 scope). The drafting queue SDR-18 gives Trajectory does not exist in code.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: On Syzygy the plane-(a) population is measurable today from files alone: 13 active changes; 151 requirement headings, 85 distinct identified requirements (CAP1 42, POC 26, PWB 17) and 64 headings with no identifier in 9 Polaris/dossier changes (B3-F7). Whether each is 'approved' is decidable from adoption rows and tags for some (30+ version tags, B3-F8) and [Unknown] for the rest without reading each change's adoption record.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: V0 plane (a) is absence surfacing, not a gap: 'approved requirement R, with no approved execution-intent Proposal and no declared motivates edge' is a listed absence, never a computed 'unbuilt' claim (v1.md: 'V0 surfaces absence; V1 computes gaps'). Rendering R as 'not implemented' would be a gap claim; rendering 'no work traceably warranted by R' is the honest V0 row. Until a warrant source exists (L1-M1/M3), every identified requirement is in this absence set, which is correct output, like the mostly-Unknown map v1.md calls 'the correct output, not a defect'.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: A requirement with no identifier cannot be a pinned warrant except by (change path, heading text, blob digest), which renames silently when the heading is edited. 64 of 151 requirement headings on Syzygy are in this state. The pre-work view should count them as 'requirements without identity' — an absence that blocks warranting — rather than drop them or mint ids for them.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: The inverse population (work items with no requirement) is the RFC8-23 Unknown-provenance count already rendered as 'governing intent Unknown 10,971 of 10,971'; the two views should be one bipartite rendering (requirements × items), with both margins counted, so the owner sees the uncovered requirements and the unwarranted work in one place. Exclusivity (RFC8-8) means a plane-(b) total must never sum two proposals in one exclusivity group; with zero proposals today, that obligation is vacuous but must be built into the count before the first proposal lands.

Count requirement headings with no identifier separately. Plane (b): enumerate `.syzygy/work/proposals/**` approved and queued-for-materialization (never 'scheduled'), queue order visible; renders an observed empty set with its denominator when the directory exists and is empty, Unknown(missing-declaration) when it is absent. No 'unbuilt', no percentage.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: The owner's daily need is a delta, not a census: 'of what merged since I last looked, which is warranted, which is evaluated, which failed'. v1.md's V1 acceptance test names it: 'At the end of an orchestration day the owner can give, from Syzygy alone, an accurate account of what the fleet changed and why, without reading raw diffs.' 'Why' is the warrant; 'accurate' is the chain state.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The released wave-1 slice for the five answers (syzygy-t3jk.16, open) specifies the fifth row as 'verified = Unknown for N of N with the governing-intent count'. Under RFC2-18 only materialized work that reached merge is in the chain (B2-F7), so that row puts every unwarranted item into a verification denominator it is not in, and merges two populations RFC8-23 and RFC2-19(a) keep apart (Unknown-provenance is a counted claim state with a reason; 'reconciliation evidence absent' is chain-state-local and never counted among Unknown reasons). It is a correction to a bead in flight, cheap now and expensive after it lands with its spec amendment and parity tests.
findings.where: `bd list --all --json` record syzygy-t3jk.16 description ('Expected content at wave 1'); RFC-0002/reconciliation-chain.md:141-160, 254-266; RFC-0008/accounting-reconciliation-and-release.md:135-156

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Four post-merge answers, never one rendering (RFC8-28): reconciled at E with evidence; merged, not yet evaluated; evaluated and unsatisfied (a gap → routes to work or upward as a spec indictment); evaluated, contradiction raised (→ owner adjudication only). Never sharing 'a mark, a mark's colour, a count, or a legend entry'; distinguishable without colour. Every aggregate over merged work carries the composition (n reconciled, m pending, k unsatisfied, c contradiction-raised, j Unknown) (RFC8-30). Two further populations sit outside the chain and must not be folded into it: Unknown-provenance merged work (RFC8-23) and orphaned-work Contradictions (RFC8-8) — the latter exempt from filtering.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: At V0, on today's data, the honest daily line is mostly zeros with denominators and one large Unknown: 'Merged since <instant>: Unknown (merge facts not read — T10/U-merge) · In the reconciliation chain: 0 · Unknown-provenance: n · Orphaned work: not detected (no predicate declared)'. That is less impressive than a board and more useful: each row is a route (read merge facts; declare warrants; declare the orphan predicate), and the row changes the day each move lands, which is how the owner sees the fifth question being built.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: What the owner does with each answer is different, which is why they cannot share a rendering: 'merged, not evaluated' → trigger an evaluation pass (human-triggered, RFC2-19); 'unsatisfied' → accept the gap as work or indict the spec; 'contradiction-raised' and orphaned work → adjudicate (since D10 an agent row can, per VIS-4's lower-rules clause — L4 recommends the owner see them first regardless); 'Unknown-provenance' → nothing per item, a warrant backfill batch per epic. A rendering that does not route each to its action fails VIS-1's comprehension value even if truthful.

proposals.title: Correct the fifth row before it lands: three populations, never 'N of N'
proposals.what: Amend syzygy-t3jk.16's expected content: the fifth row renders (i) Unknown-provenance n of N served items (reason, route: supply a warrant), (ii) in the reconciliation chain: an observed 0 with its denominator and the chain-state-local 'reconciliation evidence absent' count, never stamped with an RFC2-24 reason, (iii) orphaned-work Contradictions: Unknown(missing-declaration) — no orphan predicate declared. No 'verified' wording; no sum across the three.
changes: bead syzygy-t3jk.16 description (by the lead session)
POC spec amendment for the five answers
proposals.prereq: none (it is the slice already released)

proposals.title: The post-merge account: a since-instant ledger with RFC8-30 composition, routed per answer
proposals.what: A Trajectory section and machine answer: for a window the reader picks (since last evaluation / day / week), merged items split into the four chain answers plus Unknown-provenance and orphaned work, each a count with denominator, each expandable to identities, each with its action route; field-qualified (`chain:merged` vs `normalized:merged`, RFC8-12). At V0, chain verdicts other than pending are absent by construction; at V1 (after L2-M1) they populate.
proposals.prereq: merge facts (run-1 T10 or recorded-identity PR links, U9); the window comparison benefits from run-1 T6

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Every work item's governing intent is hard-wired Unknown at observation time, independent of any record Syzygy holds. observeWorkItems sets `governedBy: governingIntentUnknown()` on every row; the materialization record is never consulted for it. So even after run-1 move T7 runs the loop, the materialized item's card would still read 'Governing intent: Unknown' unless the observation is changed to join the record. Run 1's T7 text ('After it, one item of 10,971 has a governing intent from Syzygy's own record') is therefore not delivered by T7's slices as written [Inferred from code; T7's slices name no change to work-items.ts].

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The materialization record does not carry the warrant. The packet has `governingIntent {requirementId, proposalPath, designPath}`, but the persisted MaterializationRecord holds only beadId, externalRef, targetRepoRoot, createdAt, doltRevisionAtCreation, attribution, origin. The intent is recoverable only because externalRef and the packet are both compile-time constants for one item. No requirement revision, spec digest, adoption row or approval identity is recorded at dispatch time, so RFC8-8's materialization record join (approved intent version -> work item) cannot be reconstructed from the record if the constants change.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Two different intents govern the one demonstrated loop. The dispatch packet names REQ-switchboard-identity-001; the worker-change verification badge cites `seeds.workerChangeIntentId` = REQ-connector-base-spec-001, with a different seam (whatsapp_user_client.py vs the mapped identity.py). A run of the loop would therefore bind test evidence to an intent other than the one the item was materialized under. The split is documented as four literals in a candidate design note, not resolved.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The materialization record is local, 0600, under the daemon state dir, and becomes Observed only when the named bead is confirmed present in the same evaluation's work items. That is the right posture (record = memory, confirmation = observation) and is the only place in the code where a Syzygy-authored record is joined to a tracker fact. It is single-slot: one file, one item; the type cannot hold a second materialization.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Beads' external_ref is the only tracker-side identity Syzygy writes (as an idempotency key, `syzygy-poc:work:<slug>`), and it is queried only by the materialize action. The work-item observation's SELECT names seven columns and not external_ref, so the one structured backlink the tracker holds is not read for the board.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The verification pipeline has no Verified arm by construction: resolveTestArtifactVerification returns only `unknown` or `reported` (tier report-fact, RFC5-19). It binds a record to scope, exact changed-or-merged commit sha, exit 0, ingest-after-authored and ingest-before-evaluation. It does not bind to an intent identity, a requirement, or an acceptance criterion; the intent is supplied separately by the seed constant and only gates which Unknown text renders.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The worker-change seam's 'changed-or-merged' state is ancestry of a `[beadId]`-tagged commit to origin's default branch; the label conflates two facts RFC8-13 keeps apart (a VCS merge fact vs a change). It is scoped to one bead and two paths; it carries the commit subject (free text) in the served model.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: A reconciliation verdict type already exists, in cap1-core and nowhere in the POC: `ReconciliationFacts` (computed false -> each merged work item renders 'reconciliation evidence absent'; computed true -> satisfied|unsatisfied for a declaredScope) and `computeReconciled` mapping to Unknown / Gap / satisfied; drawer.ts defines `ChainState` = merged | reconciliation-pending | reconciled@E | unsatisfied | contradiction-raised | Unknown(r) per RFC2-18. No non-test producer supplies ReconciliationFacts: a sweep of packages/*/src and apps/*/src (non-test .ts) for `reconciliation:`, `computed: true` and `mergedWork` outside facets.ts returned 0 lines; a second method (Python re over 310 non-test .ts files under packages/*/src and apps/*/src, excluding facets.ts, for ReconciliationFacts|computeReconciled|mergedWork) also returned 0 files. So the vocabulary is built and the input is never produced.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Proposed work (the pre-work plane substrate) is one followed OpenSpec change, with lifecycle read from tree paths (active / archived / contradicted / unresolvable) and the current authority looked up in the observed shape. It is a single seeded change, not an enumeration of a project's changes, and it carries no link to any work item.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Seed graph relationships `materializes-as`, `changes`, `verified-by`, `satisfies-at-runtime` exist as declared seed edges with per-edge epistemics; `materializes-as` is Observed only from the confirmed materialization record. These are hand-declared for one capability, so the RFC1 relation vocabulary exists in the POC only as a demo graph.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The write that would create the first warranted item is foreclosed in code by P-71-Q5 before any registry entry is read (`FORECLOSED_EFFECTS`), and `dispatchAuthorization()` passes a null entry. Already known as run-1 T7 and syzygy-mxas; recorded here only as a prerequisite edge for every Syzygy-created warrant.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The chain the fifth question walks is fixed verbatim by RFC8-21: "warrant (normative reference or Decision) → approved plan item (execution-intent Proposal) → materialization record → work item → execution run(s) → commits/PR → merge fact → reconciliation verdict", each link "rendered with its declared basis (`recorded-identity` vs `naming-convention`, the latter `reduced-fidelity`)", and "That thinness must render as thinness". RFC8-22: "Where a link cannot be established at the answering evaluation, the chain renders the break at that link — Unknown with its RFC2-24 reason" and "Reconstructing a join by similarity, interpolation, or inference is forbidden".

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The materialization record must hold three things: RFC8-10 "proposal identity, work-item identity set, and the pinned warranted intent revision (RFC1-29; RFC1-5), all three required, none conditional"; RFC1-29 "pinning the exact intent revision — requirement, scenario, or governance clause version — cited by the proposal's warrant". The POC's MaterializationRecord holds none of the first or third (see B1-F2), and it lives in the daemon state dir, whereas SDR-7 places approved intent and the record under `.syzygy/work/**` and RFC8-26 lists "materialization mappings" in the binding preservation set. A record in a 0600 file under a state dir is neither the RFC8-10 record nor preserved under RFC8-26.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: The contract does not state the predicate that separates an orphaned-work Contradiction from an Unknown-provenance item. RFC1-29: "Scheduler work items matching no materialization record are an orphaned-work contradiction"; RFC8-8 repeats it unconditionally. RFC8-23: "An Unknown-provenance item may be legitimate untraceable work — a pre-Syzygy backlog item, an import" and "Unknown-provenance is not orphaned work". Read literally, every one of the proving project's 10,971 items (none has a record) is an orphaned-work Contradiction routed to adjudication, "exempt from filtering"; read by RFC8-23, they are Unknown-provenance. Nothing in RFC1-29, RFC8-8, RFC8-10 or RFC8-23 names what makes an item 'pre-Syzygy'. The POC spec defers it explicitly: POC-REQ-014 "makes no claim about orphaned work: the POC detects none … left to the amendment that specifies orphaned-work detection". This is the first decision any warrant work must make, and it decides whether Trajectory's default state for imported work is a counted badge or 10,971 Contradictions.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The tracker is never the warrant. RFC4-15: Beads' authority is "work lifecycle state, after materialization only (SDR-7) — never intent, never observed behavior, never why the work exists". RFC4-17: at materialization the adapter writes the warrant reference into `spec_id`/metadata "as a derived, re-derivable pointer"; "the `.syzygy/work/**` materialization record stays authoritative"; a substrate-side edit renders as an annotation. RFC8-23 repeats: "A substrate-side warrant-field edit is an annotation, not a competing warrant". So any tracker field (spec_id, external_ref, labels, title text) can at most be a pointer Syzygy wrote or an annotation; read alone it cannot lawfully establish a warrant.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: `motivates` may run straight to a work item, not only through a Proposal: RFC1-25's row reads "Requirement ref · Decision · Policy → Work item · Proposal; Gap → only through a confirmation act", class "Desired → execution (the work-warrant edge)", carrying the four warrant classes "{approved requirement/intent, confirmed finding, declared policy, explicit owner decision}". A Decision that declares `motivates` edges onto existing items is therefore a lawful warrant source for pre-existing work, distinct from materialization. RFC1-26: "A relation may be added to this table only by amendment carrying an owner decision" — so no new relation is needed or allowed for warrant backfill; `motivates` already exists.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Adapter-owned join bases in RFC4-22 cover "work item ↔ branch/worktree, branch → commits, commit → PR, PR → merge fact, gate outcome → artifact" — not warrant → work item. A requirement id parsed from a commit subject or PR body is therefore not a declared RFC4-22 join for the warrant link; at most it is naming-convention evidence for commit ↔ work item, and for the warrant link it is execution-side prose, which RFC8-25 forbids as a warrant source: "A warrant is never extended by execution-side prose".

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The reconciliation chain applies only to materialized work: RFC2-18 "Every materialized work item that reaches merge enters a first-class chain on its durable identity". Merged work with no warrant is RFC8-23 Unknown-provenance, not `reconciliation-pending`. Consequence: on the proving project today the chain has an empty population; a fifth-question row of the form 'verified 0 of N' (run-1 T3 says "verified (0 of N)") would put 10,971 Unknown-provenance items in a denominator they are not in. The honest V0 rows are: Unknown-provenance n; in chain 0; of those, reconciliation evidence absent 0.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: `reconciled@E` needs gate-backed Observed evidence (RFC2-18 "a positive status claim requiring gate-backed Observed evidence (RFC2-25)"; RFC2-25 gate-backed is "The only tier that may support a positive status claim"). RFC4-13 admits gate-backed through exactly one of four routes: (1) a Syzygy-launched profiled run; (2) external CI/hosting whose run identity and authenticity the sub-adapter confirmed at observation time and captured per RFC4-13(a); (3) an owner-declared trusted-external-oracle policy scoped to a (project, gate class) pair with expiry; (4) a governed checker for doc-only and governance-only work. The POC's operator-reported JUnit is none of these and correctly caps at report-fact.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: V0 vs V1 for the verdict: RFC8-29 "V0 renders the absence honestly … every merged-but-unreconciled item renders 'reconciliation evidence absent / Unknown' … Nothing in V0 simulates a verdict. V1 computes the reconciliation evaluation". RFC2-19(a) (ratified as SDR-34 per DECISION-HISTORY P-31) makes that rendering chain-state-local: "never stamped with, counted among, or absorbed by an aggregate of RFC2-24 Unknown reasons". cap1-core already encodes this split (`MERGED_WORK_UNRECONCILED_STATE`), but cap1's computeReconciled returns the Unknown render with reason MISSING_EVIDENCE for the uncomputed case, and keeps each merged item's 'reconciliation evidence absent' as a separate served fact; its comment (facets.ts:664-668) says this is deliberate (the facet answer is a claim, the per-item value is the chain-state-local fact). [Inferred] consistent with RFC2-19(a), which says #2 missing-evidence "misdescribes a verdict never sought" only for the per-item rendering; a Trajectory reuse must keep the same split.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The four post-merge answers must never share a rendering: RFC8-28 "*reconciled at E with evidence* vs *merged, not yet evaluated* vs *evaluated and unsatisfied* vs *evaluated, contradiction raised* are four different answers and must never share a rendering", "never share a mark, a mark's colour, a count, or a legend entry", and the chain state is "a field of its own" that travels beside the normalized state on every rendering, filter, count and endpoint. RFC8-30: progress aggregates over merged work "disclose their reconciliation composition (n reconciled, m pending, k unsatisfied, c contradiction-raised, j Unknown)".

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Pre-work plane obligations: RFC8-8(a) approved normative claims covered by no approved execution-intent Proposal — "at V0 this is absence surfacing, not gap computation"; (b) approved execution intent not yet materialized — "from `.syzygy/work/**`, queue order visible"; (c) open materialized items each checked against the record. RFC8-7: lifecycle drafted → under review → approved → queued-for-materialization → materialized; queued is "a recorded queue act in `.syzygy/work/**`", "never named 'scheduled'". Drafts render `unadopted draft` and never count. Exclusivity: no total may sum two proposals in one exclusivity group. `.syzygy/work/` does not exist in Syzygy's own tree (ls at 9ebf12476: governance, intent, map only).

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Review lane: RFC8-13 `review` = "An open review lane bound to an exact head SHA", derived from "Open PR facts (hosting sub-adapter) + review work item/labels + `external_ref`"; "reviewer activity is never claimed"; "a merge-readiness verdict binds to its head SHA and expires when the head moves". RFC4-11's hosting sub-adapter reads PR identity, head SHA, base, state, created/merged instants, review decision, review threads, check conclusions, and merge facts: "A merge fact comes only from this adapter — never inferred from scheduler closure". Squash-plus-delete merges make per-commit facts unreachable → PR-granularity reduced-fidelity, cause `post-merge-history-unreachable`.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Retention constrains the join: RFC4-16(2) "Every scheduler-resident fact a durable Syzygy record depends on — the run envelope's inputs, materialization joins, transition history feeding an account — must be captured into Syzygy-owned artifacts … before the horizon"; RFC8-26 preserves "work warrants, decisions, materialization mappings … evidence identities and hashes, and reconciliation outcomes"; RFC8-27 "a preserved hash with no capture artifact and no other satisfied route caps at `report-fact`". So the warrant join and any gate capture must be Syzygy-owned and git-durable from day one; a daemon state-dir file satisfies none of these.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: VIS-4's 'Lower rules follow this one' reaches the contract's owner-adjudication exits. RFC8-8 routes orphaned work to "owner adjudication as its only lawful exit"; RFC4-13 route 3 and RFC4-23/RFC8-16 bounds are "honored only under RFC3-16(a)". None is in VIS-4's four classes, so an agent adoption row now satisfies them. That makes warrant backfill and orphan adjudication mechanically cheap — and removes the separation between the agent that did the work and the authority that says what it was for. The doctrine permits it; the fifth question's credibility depends on not letting the same session warrant and verify its own work.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The Beads issues table has 56 columns, among them two structured warrant-capable fields: `spec_id` (the field RFC4-17 names for the warrant pointer) and `external_ref`, plus `metadata` (JSON). Others relevant: assignee, created_by, owner, closed_by_session, close_reason, started_at, last_activity, compaction_level, source_system, source_repo, work_type.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: spec_id is non-empty on 26 of 1,370 items (1.9%). Of the 26: 19 begin `openspec/`, 18 contain `.md`, 0 match a requirement-id grammar `^[A-Z0-9]+-REQ-[0-9]+`, 21 match a plain identifier/path grammar `^[A-Za-z0-9._:/#-]+$` (5 do not; max length 128). So the field RFC4-17 reserves for the warrant pointer is used ad hoc, as a change/spec path, never as a requirement anchor, and never written by Syzygy.
findings.where: SQL: SUM(spec_id REGEXP ...), SUM(spec_id LIKE 'openspec/%') over issues WHERE spec_id<>''

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: external_ref is non-empty on 216 of 1,370 items (15.8%): 192 `gh-pr:N`, 22 `gh-NNN` (one per item, prefixes gh-302..gh-332), 2 `https…`. So the tracker already holds a recorded-identity work item → PR link for 192 items (an actor wrote the PR number), which is the RFC4-22 `recorded-identity` basis for the work item ↔ PR link, and the RFC8-13 `review` row's `external_ref` input. It carries nothing about intent.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: metadata is a non-empty JSON object on 37 of 1,370 items, with ~40 distinct ad-hoc keys (review_receipt 19, implementation_authorized 8, readiness_audit 7, completed_review_receipt 7, workstream_role 5; singletons include signed_spec_tag, authorization_record, approval_date, acceptance_result). Agents already record warrant- and verification-shaped facts per item, with no schema, no declared grammar and no Syzygy reader. [Inferred] they are worker-asserted (RFC8-25 asserted-by-worker) and could not serve as a warrant or gate outcome as they stand.
findings.where: SQL: JSON_KEYS(metadata) WHERE JSON_LENGTH(metadata)>0, key frequencies computed in Python

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Edges: 1,633 dependency rows (860 blocks, 665 parent-child, 79 discovered-from, 14 relates-to, 10 related, 5 tracks); 3,538 label rows over 1,117 items. None of the six edge types is a warrant edge. (Run 1 measured 1,580 edges at its time; the tracker grew.)
findings.where: SQL: dependencies GROUP BY type; labels COUNT

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Closure facts: 945 items closed, 933 carry a close_reason (text not read). acceptance_criteria non-empty on 779 items (text not read). compaction_level > 0 on 0 items: no Beads compaction has run on this tracker yet, so RFC4-16 horizon loss is not yet a measured problem here.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: OpenSpec: 13 active changes, 1 archived, 0 baseline `openspec/specs/*/spec.md`. 151 `Requirement:` headings in change specs; 87 carry an id (CAP1-REQ 44 headings / 42 distinct in the CAP1 change plus 2 in cap1-trusted-bootstrap-consent, PWB-REQ 17, POC-REQ 26; 85 distinct ids), and 64 headings in 9 Polaris/dossier changes carry no id at all (e.g. 'Requirement: Admitted project input'). A requirement without an identifier cannot be a pinned warrant revision except by heading text plus file digest.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Spec version tags exist for 30+ amendments and Polaris specs, but none for the base CAP1 change (project-registration-and-honest-shape-visibility) or the base three-surface-poc change (`git tag -l`, 65 tags). A pinned intent revision for a CAP1 or base POC requirement would have to be a commit plus file blob digest, not a tag.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: tasks.md ↔ bead links are sparse: 13 tasks.md files, 199 checkbox tasks in all, bead ids named in 5 of them (7 distinct-id mentions in total). OpenSpec tasks are not the plan items the tracker executes.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Commit subjects, last 500 on origin/main to c813f041c: 365 carry a bracketed `[syzygy-…]` token (448 any bead id; 64 are merge commits), 1 carries a CAP1/POC/PWB requirement id, 0 carry both. Second method (`git log --format=%s | grep -cE`) gives the same 1 and 365. Commit bodies: 1 of 500 names a requirement id. So item ↔ commit has a strong naming convention; requirement ↔ commit has effectively none.
findings.where: git log c813f041c -500; Python re and grep -cE

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Merged PRs #593..#843 (200): 138 bodies name a bead id, 179 head branches name one, 7 bodies name a requirement id; every one has a merge commit. With B3-F3, the item ↔ PR ↔ merge-fact links are recoverable at scale (recorded identity for 192 items, naming convention for most of the rest); the requirement end is not.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Gate evidence on GitHub: main's head merge commit c813f041c (PR #840) carries 9 GitHub Actions check runs, all `success` (node unit/integration/e2e, governance and selftest checks), on that exact SHA. node-ci.yml runs on pull_request and merge_group only ('No push trigger … main moves only through the merge queue, whose merge_group run already tested the exact tree that lands'). It uploads no per-test report artifact (no upload-artifact, no JUnit reporter in the file). So RFC4-13 route 2 (hosting-confirmed run identity) is available per merge commit at job granularity; per-requirement granularity needs a retained per-test report.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: CAP1 has exactly one conformance file per requirement: 42 CAP1-REQ ids in the CAP1 change, 42 `req-NNN.conformance.test.ts` files, no id without a file and no file without an id. Each file states Case / Observable / Oracle / Falsifier in its head comment (e.g. req-037). This is a declared, 1:1 requirement → test mapping already in the tree.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: docs/evidence holds 6,182 files (3,406 .json); 2,372 contain a 40-hex SHA; 379 name a CAP1/POC/PWB requirement id; 11 contain a JUnit `<testsuite`. Evidence is plentiful, revision-bound by convention, and not indexed by requirement or work item; it is report-fact at best (written by sessions, not captured by a hosting-confirmed route).

findings.label: Unknown
findings.text: Butlers (proving project): its tracker's spec_id / external_ref / metadata population, its commit-subject convention, its PR↔bead linkage, its CI and its requirement-id density are not readable from this session. Run 1 recorded 10,971 items and the requirement id REQ-switchboard-identity-001 exists in its openspec (seed constant), but nothing here measures them.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: The most likely false 'verified' is adjacency of constants, and the trap is still armed. The one recorded incident (AGENTS.md note; M8 funnel: "That produced a false 'Verified' once and was reverted") came from wiring test-artifact evidence into the wrong entities because the constant groups sit together. Today the verification badge's intent is a third seed literal (`workerChangeIntentId` = REQ-connector-base-spec-001) that no record joins to the materialized item, whose packet names REQ-switchboard-identity-001 (B1-F3). The guard is only that no Verified arm exists. The first change that adds one (any V1 reconciliation move, U-moves included) inherits a verdict bound to an intent the record never pinned. The fix is structural: the verdict must read the intent from the materialization record (or declared motivates edge) of that item, and the seed literal must be deleted, not re-pointed.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: An Observed `governed-by` edge cites a provenance location that no longer exists. `capability-to-intent` renders `observed('The relationship is declared by the bounded POC mapping.')` with mappingProvenance source `packages/three-surface-poc-core/src/model.ts#ARTIFACT_PATHS`; ARTIFACT_PATHS occurs in exactly two lines across packages/three-surface-poc-core/src and apps/three-surface-poc/src (non-test), both in model-slices.ts (the digest key and this string); model.ts defines no such symbol; the seeds live in poc-seeds.ts. The digest is computed from the live seeds, so the bytes are bound, but the route a reader follows does not resolve (RFC1-26: "Every rendered internal edge must resolve to its identified target"). It also shows the warrant edge is declared in implementation code, not in a governance mapping artifact (SDR-4: "governance mapping artifacts are the primary declaration site").

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: Green CI is the easiest route to a false `reconciled@E` at V1. On Syzygy every merge commit carries all-success check runs (u3 B3-F12) that are job-level. 'The unit tier passed on merge commit M' is a true gate-backed fact (RFC4-13 route 2) about the suite, not about requirement R; SDR-3: "A passing test does not by itself prove semantic ownership". A verdict needs (a) a declared requirement → check mapping (a governance artifact, not a filename convention), (b) the per-test outcome of that check at M, retained, and (c) evidence that the check can fail for R (rule 6 mutation evidence). Without (a)–(c), job-green must cap at report-fact for R or render Unknown(mapping-coverage-absent).

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: Worker-written metadata is a ready-made false-green source. 37 Syzygy items carry ad-hoc metadata keys such as acceptance_result, review_receipt, implementation_authorized, signed_spec_tag (B3-F4). If a future reader admits metadata, each value is a worker assertion: RFC2-25 `asserted-by-worker` ("never a status input") or, with a retained artifact the worker wrote, report-fact (RFC4-13 violation case 6: a well-formed report a worker left on disk "emitted `gate-backed` because it is retained, resolvable, and hash-carrying — origin unverified"). None of these keys can serve as a warrant either: RFC8-25 "A warrant is never extended by execution-side prose".

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: Self-warranting. Under VIS-4's 'Lower rules follow this one', an agent row satisfies orphan adjudication and warrant declaration (B2-F14). A session that writes a warrant row for its own item, merges it, and reads its own CI green has produced warrant, merge and gate with no independent party. Doctrine allows it; the fifth question's value is that 'a merged change is not a satisfied intent', which collapses if the warrant is authored after the fact by the worker. The check that keeps it honest is mechanical: a warrant's adoption commit must precede the item's first commit (or the warrant renders `declared-after-work`, a distinct state), and the adopter identity must differ from the item's claimant, else the edge renders asserted-by-worker.
findings.where: .syzygy/governance/doctrine/vision.md:206-212; README north star (quoted in run-1 dossier:26-28)

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: The materialization record mis-dates reuse. When the local record is missing and the bead is found by external_ref, the new record is written with `createdAt: input.now()` and `doltRevisionAtCreation` captured now, with `origin: 'reused'`. The dispatch disclosure then serves that instant as the dispatched `createdAt`. The bead's own created_at (a tracker fact) is not used. Small, but it is exactly the RFC8-10 'materializing evaluation' that must be correct for the one-way door.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: Two weaker time checks in the verification resolver: it compares the ingest instant to the commit's author date (`%aI`), which the author sets freely, rather than the committer date; and an unparseable evaluationAsOf silently skips the future-dated check (`!Number.isNaN(evaluationAsOfMs) && …`). Neither produces a false Verified today (no Verified arm), but both are fail-open predicates a V1 gate would inherit.

findings.label: Observed
findings.text: 'Changed / merged' is one label for two facts, and the merge half is ancestry of a bead-tagged commit to origin's default branch found with `git log --all` (which also searches local branches and any other ref). RFC8-13 reserves `merged` for "A VCS merge fact only (RFC4-11)", which comes from the hosting sub-adapter's merge facts. Ancestry is a reasonable merge proxy, but it is a naming-convention join (the `[beadId]` grep) and should render reduced-fidelity, cause derived-from-convention (RFC4-22), which the seam does not.

findings.label: Inferred
findings.text: A fifth-question count with the wrong denominator is the most likely false claim at V0 (not a false green, a false number). 'Verified 0 of 10,971' implies 10,971 items awaiting verification; under RFC2-18 only materialized-and-merged items are in the chain (B2-F7). The honest V0 count is three disjoint populations: Unknown-provenance (no warrant), in-chain with 'reconciliation evidence absent' (chain-state-local, RFC2-19(a)), and orphaned-work Contradictions (once the predicate exists), never summed.
